So Moses told the judges of Israel, “Each of you must kill all of his men who have joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.” (25:5).
Just then an Israelite man brought to his family a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation of Israel while they were weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. (25:6).
On seeing this, Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, got up from the assembly, took a spear in his hand, (25:7).
followed the Israelite into the tent, and drove the spear through both of them— through the Israelite and on through the belly of the woman. So the plague against the Israelites was halted, (25:8).
but those who died in the plague numbered 24,000. (25:9).
Then the LORD said to Moses, (25:10).

“Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the Israelites; for he was zealous for My sake among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in My zeal. (25:11).
Declare, therefore, that I am granting him My covenant of peace. (25:12).
It will be a covenant of permanent priesthood for him and his descendants, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.” (25:13).
The name of the Israelite who was slain with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a Simeonite family. (25:14).
And the name of the slain Midianite woman was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a Midianite family. (25:15).
And the LORD said to Moses, (25:16).
“Attack the Midianites and strike them dead. (25:17).

For they assailed you deceitfully when they seduced you in the matter of Peor and their sister Cozbi, the daughter of the Midianite leader, the woman who was killed on the day the plague came because of Peor.” (25:18).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 4:3: Your own eyes saw what the LORD did at Baal-peor; He destroyed everyone who followed it.
Psalm 106:28-31: They yoked themselves to Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to lifeless gods.
Hosea 9:10: They came to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to that shameful thing.
Numbers 31:15-16: The women of Midian named as the cause, acting on Balaam's advice.
Revelation 2:14: Balaam taught Balak to put a stumbling block before Israel, to eat food sacrificed to idols and commit immorality.

translationNotes.note: Baal means lord or master, and it is the title of the storm god of Canaan and the wider region, also called Hadad, whose worship existed to secure rain and fertility for fields, herds and families. Peor is the mountain in Moab where this local form of him was served (23:28). Worship centred on sacrificial meals at high places, and the fertility theme carried into sexual rites, which is what verses 1 and 2 describe happening together: immorality with the women, then an invitation to the sacrifices, then eating and bowing down. Elsewhere Scripture reports what else the cult ran to: prophets of Baal gashing themselves with swords and lances until blood ran (1 Kings 18:28), and high places of Baal where sons were burned in the fire as offerings, which the LORD says He never commanded and which never entered His mind (Jeremiah 19:5; 32:35).

The verb means to be harnessed or strapped to something, from the noun tzemed, a yoked pair of oxen. Psalm 106:28 keeps the image: they yoked themselves to Baal of Peor. It is not the language of an opinion or a phase but of being hitched to a load, and the same word supplies the picture Paul draws on for being unequally yoked.

Eating the sacrifice was the act of joining the cult, not a meal on the side. The worshipper's portion of an offering was eaten in the sanctuary precinct, so sharing it made a man a participant. That is the whole issue behind the question of food sacrificed to idols in 1 Corinthians 8 and 10, and Revelation 2:14 names this incident when it raises it.

A romach is a heavy thrusting lance, not a javelin. The place Phinehas follows them into is called a qubbah, a word found nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible, understood as an inner chamber or a tent alcove. The offence he is answering is not private: Zimri brings a Midianite chief's daughter into the camp in front of Moses and the whole assembly while the people are weeping at the entrance of the tent (25:6).

The text names both and gives both their rank (25:14-15): Zimri son of Salu is the head of a Simeonite family, and Cozbi is the daughter of Zur, one of the five Midianite chiefs later killed at 31:8. This is not two nobodies. It is a leader of an Israelite clan pairing with the daughter of a Midianite ruling house at the exact moment Israel is being drawn into that country's cult, which is why chapter 31 follows.

The grant to Phinehas is a lasting priesthood for him and his line (25:12-13). It held: Phinehas is the priest at Bethel in Judges 20:28, and the high priestly line traced through him serves down to the exile (1 Chronicles 6:4-15). Psalm 106:31 says the act was credited to him as righteousness, using the same formula used of Abraham in Genesis 15:6.

stories.keyTakeaway: Israelite men engage in sexual immorality with Moabite women and worship their gods, bringing divine anger; Phinehas kills an Israelite man and Midianite woman during the resulting plague, earning a covenant of lasting priesthood for turning God's anger away.

“Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by the houses of their fathers — all those twenty years of age or older who can serve in the army of Israel.” (26:2).
So on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest issued the instruction, (26:3).
“Take a census of the men twenty years of age or older, as the LORD has commanded Moses.” And these were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt: (26:4).
Reuben was the firstborn of Israel. These were the descendants of Reuben: The Hanochite clan from Hanoch, the Palluite clan from Pallu, (26:5).
the Hezronite clan from Hezron, and the Carmite clan from Carmi. (26:6).
These were the clans of Reuben, and their registration numbered 43,730. (26:7).
Now the son of Pallu was Eliab, (26:8).

and the sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. It was Dathan and Abiram, chosen by the congregation, who rebelled against Moses and Aaron with the followers of Korah who rebelled against the LORD. (26:9).
And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, whose followers died when the fire consumed 250 men. They serve as a warning sign. (26:10).
However, the line of Korah did not die out. (26:11).
These were the descendants of Simeon by their clans: The Nemuelite clan from Nemuel, the Jaminite clan from Jamin, the Jachinite clan from Jachin, (26:12).
the Zerahite clan from Zerah, and the Shaulite clan from Shaul. (26:13).

These were the clans of Judah, and their registration numbered . . . 76,500. (26:22).

the Jashubite clan from Jashub, and the Shimronite clan from Shimron. (26:24).
These were the clans of Issachar, and their registration numbered . . . 64,300. (26:25).
These were the descendants of Zebulun by their clans: The Seredite clan from Sered, the Elonite clan from Elon, and the Jahleelite clan from Jahleel. (26:26).
These were the clans of Zebulun, and their registration numbered . . . 60,500. (26:27).
The descendants of Joseph included the clans of Manasseh and Ephraim. (26:28).
These were the descendants of Manasseh: The Machirite clan from Machir, the father of Gilead, and the Gileadite clan from Gilead. (26:29).
These were the descendants of Gilead: the Iezerite clan from Iezer, the Helekite clan from Helek, (26:30).
