And the descendants of Shuthelah were the Eranite clan from Eran. (26:36).
These were the clans of Ephraim, and their registration numbered . . . 32,500. These clans were the descendants of Joseph. (26:37).
These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans: The Belaite clan from Bela, the Ashbelite clan from Ashbel, the Ahiramite clan from Ahiram, (26:38).
the Shuphamite clan from Shupham, and the Huphamite clan from Hupham. (26:39).
And the descendants of Bela from Ard and Naaman were the Ardite clan from Ard and the Naamite clan from Naaman. (26:40).
These were the clans of Benjamin, and their registration numbered . . . 45,600. (26:41).
These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: The Shuhamite clan from Shuham. These were the clans of Dan. (26:42).
All of them were Shuhamite clans, and their registration numbered . . . 64,400. (26:43).
These were the descendants of Asher by their clans: The Imnite clan from Imnah, the Ishvite clan from Ishvi, and the Beriite clan from Beriah. (26:44).
And these were the descendants of Beriah: the Heberite clan from Heber and the Malchielite clan from Malchiel. (26:45).
And the name of Asher’s daughter was Serah. (26:46).
These were the clans of Asher, and their registration numbered . . . 53,400. (26:47).
These were the descendants of Naphtali by their clans: The Jahzeelite clan from Jahzeel, the Gunite clan from Guni, (26:48).
the Jezerite clan from Jezer, and the Shillemite clan from Shillem. (26:49).
These were the clans of Naphtali, and their registration numbered . . . 45,400. (26:50).
These men of Israel numbered 601,730 in all. (26:51).
Then the LORD said to Moses, (26:52).
“The land is to be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, according to the number of names. (26:53).
Increase the inheritance for a large tribe and decrease it for a small one; each tribe is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those registered. (26:54).
Indeed, the land must be divided by lot; they shall receive their inheritance according to the names of the tribes of their fathers. (26:55).
Each inheritance is to be divided by lot among the larger and smaller tribes.” (26:56).
Now these were the Levites numbered by their clans: The Gershonite clan from Gershon, the Kohathite clan from Kohath, and the Merarite clan from Merari. (26:57).
These were the families of the Levites: The Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, and the Korahite clan. Now Kohath was the father of Amram, (26:58).
and Amram’s wife was named Jochebed. She was also a daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. To Amram she bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam. (26:59).
Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were born to Aaron, (26:60).
but Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD. (26:61).

The registration of the Levites totaled 23,000, every male a month old or more; they were not numbered among the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites. (26:62).
These were the ones numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest when they counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho. (26:63).
Among all these, however, there was not one who had been numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai. (26:64).
For the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness. Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. (26:65).
crossRefs: Numbers 1:44-46: The first census in the Wilderness of Sinai returned 603,550 men of fighting age.
Numbers 14:29-32: God's oath that everyone counted in the first census would fall in the wilderness.
Joshua 14:1-2: The land divided by lot among the tribes by Eleazar, Joshua and the heads of the families.
1 Chronicles 6:31-38: Heman the singer, set over the music by David, traced back through Korah to Levi.
Numbers 27:1-7: The daughters of Zelophehad, listed by name here, bring their claim before Moses.

translationNotes.note: The second count comes to 601,730 against the first count's 603,550, a drop of 1,820 across thirty-eight years, and it counts an entirely different set of men: every one from the first census except Caleb and Joshua has died (26:64-65). Simeon falls hardest, from 59,300 to 22,200, and Manasseh rises most, from 32,200 to 52,700. The purpose is stated in verses 52 to 56: this roll, not the old one, is what the land will be divided by.

The allotment worked in two steps. The size of each tribe's share was fixed by its number in this census, larger tribes getting more land, and then the lot decided which piece of country each tribe got (26:54-56). Lots were physical objects, stones or marked pieces, drawn or shaken out of a container; Proverbs 16:33 says the lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

translationNotes.term: The line of Korah did not die out
translationNotes.note: Verse 11 is a single sentence with long consequences. Korah's sons were not swallowed up with him, and their descendants became temple singers and gatekeepers: Heman the singer is traced back through Korah in 1 Chronicles 6:33-37, and eleven psalms carry the heading of the sons of Korah, among them Psalms 42, 44 to 49 and 84.

The chapter is not a list of individuals but of clans, each named for a founding ancestor, and the counts are given by clan. This was the working unit of Israelite society between the household and the tribe: it held land together, supplied the kinsman-redeemer, and provided the men who answered a muster. Achan is identified through exactly this ladder, tribe then clan then household then man (Joshua 7:16-18).

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses and Eleazar conduct a census of Israel on the plains of Moab, recording 601,730 men twenty years old or more across the twelve tribes; the LORD instructs that land inheritance be distributed by lot according to population size. The Levites are counted separately at 23,000 and receive no land inheritance; notably, none of the original generation counted in the wilderness remain except Caleb and Joshua.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 27
summaryBullets: Now the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They approached (27:1).
the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation, and said, (27:2).
“Our father died in the wilderness, but he was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD. Instead, he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons. (27:3).
Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan because he had no sons? Give us property among our father’s brothers.” (27:4).
So Moses brought their case before the LORD, (27:5).
and the LORD answered him, (27:6).
“The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly. You certainly must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers and transfer their father’s inheritance to them. (27:7).
Furthermore, you shall say to the Israelites, ‘If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter. (27:8).
If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers. (27:9).
If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father’s brothers. (27:10).

And if his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to the next of kin from his clan, that he may take possession of it. This is to be a statutory ordinance for the Israelites, as the LORD has commanded Moses.’” (27:11).
Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites. (27:12).
After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was; (27:13).

for when the congregation contended in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters.” Those were the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin. (27:14).
So Moses appealed to the LORD, (27:15).
“May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation (27:16).
who will go out and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd.” (27:17).
And the LORD replied to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him. (27:18).
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight. (27:19).
Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him. (27:20).

He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim. At his command, he and all the Israelites with him— the entire congregation— will go out and come in.” (27:21).
Moses did as the LORD had commanded him. He took Joshua, had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, (27:22).
and laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had instructed through Moses. (27:23).
crossRefs: Numbers 36:1-12: The follow-up ruling, that an heiress must marry inside her own tribe.
Deuteronomy 34:1-5: Moses climbs Nebo, is shown the whole land, and dies there in the land of Moab.
Exodus 28:30: The Urim and the Thummim placed in the breastpiece of judgment, over Aaron's heart.
1 Samuel 28:6: Saul inquires of the LORD, who does not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets.
Deuteronomy 34:9: Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him.

translationNotes.note: Nachalah is not money left in a will. It is the family's allotted piece of land, held permanently and returned to the family at the jubilee even if sold (Leviticus 25:23-28). Losing it meant the family ceased to exist as a unit in Israel, which is exactly the argument the daughters make in verse 4: why should our father's name disappear from his clan? Naboth refuses to sell his for the same reason (1 Kings 21:3).

Two objects kept in the fold of the high priest's breastpiece, used to obtain a yes or no from God on a question put to Him (Exodus 28:30; 1 Samuel 14:41). Scripture never describes what they looked like or how they worked. Their use fades out: Saul gets no answer by them (1 Samuel 28:6), and the returning exiles set aside a question until a priest with Urim and Thummim should arise (Ezra 2:63).

The same verb and gesture used when a worshipper leans his hands on the head of a sacrifice (Leviticus 1:4) and when Israel presents the Levites (Numbers 8:10). It transfers an office or an identification in public view. Verse 20 says Moses is to put some of his authority on Joshua, and Deuteronomy 34:9 records the result. This is the root of ordination by the laying on of hands.

The escarpment on the eastern side of the Jordan valley, whose best-known summit is Nebo, about 700 metres above sea level. It stands nearly a kilometre above the valley floor below, which is around 250 metres below sea level at that point, so the whole width of Canaan is visible from it on a clear day. That is why Moses is sent up it in verse 12 and again in Deuteronomy 34:1.

stories.keyTakeaway: Zelophehad's daughters petition Moses for their father's inheritance since he had no sons; God grants their request and establishes inheritance law for daughters. God tells Moses he will die after viewing the promised land from the Abarim Range, then commands him to commission Joshua as his successor.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 28
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (28:1).
“Command the Israelites and say to them: See that you present to Me at its appointed time the food for My food offerings, as a pleasing aroma to Me. (28:2).
And tell them that this is the food offering you are to present to the LORD as a regular burnt offering each day: two unblemished year-old male lambs. (28:3).
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight, (28:4).
along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives. (28:5).
This is a regular burnt offering established at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD. (28:6).
The drink offering accompanying each lamb shall be a quarter hin. Pour out the offering of fermented drink to the LORD in the sanctuary area. (28:7).
And offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. (28:8).
On the Sabbath day, present two unblemished year-old male lambs, accompanied by a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, as well as a drink offering. (28:9).
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering. (28:10).
At the beginning of every month, you are to present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (28:11).
along with three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with the ram, (28:12).
and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each lamb. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD. (28:13).

Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine with each bull, a third of a hin with the ram, and a quarter hin with each lamb. This is the monthly burnt offering to be made at each new moon throughout the year. (28:14).
In addition to the regular burnt offering with its drink offering, one male goat is to be presented to the LORD as a sin offering. (28:15).
The fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD’s Passover. (28:16).
On the fifteenth day of this month, there shall be a feast; for seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten. (28:17).
On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work. (28:18).
Present to the LORD a food offering, a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished. (28:19).
The grain offering shall consist of fine flour mixed with oil; offer three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram, (28:20).
and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs. (28:21).
Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you. (28:22).
You are to present these in addition to the regular morning burnt offering. (28:23).
Offer the same food each day for seven days as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It is to be offered with its drink offering and the regular burnt offering. (28:24).
On the seventh day you shall hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work. (28:25).
On the day of firstfruits, when you present an offering of new grain to the LORD during the Feast of Weeks, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work. (28:26).
Present a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, (28:27).
together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram, (28:28).
and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs. (28:29).
Include one male goat to make atonement for you. (28:30).
Offer them with their drink offerings in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. The animals must be unblemished. (28:31).
crossRefs: Exodus 29:38-42: The two lambs to be offered daily at the altar, one in the morning and one at twilight.
Leviticus 23:4-21: The appointed feasts set out in order with their sacred assemblies.
1 Kings 18:29,36: Elijah acts on Carmel at the time of the evening offering.
Daniel 9:21: Gabriel reaches Daniel about the time of the evening sacrifice.
Ezekiel 46:13-15: A year-old lamb without blemish provided every morning as a burnt offering.

translationNotes.note: The tamid, the standing offering: two year-old lambs every day of the year, one at dawn and one at dusk, with their grain and drink offerings. Everything else in chapters 28 and 29 is added on top of it and never replaces it. Because it happened at fixed hours it worked as the nation's clock, which is why Elijah acts at the time of the evening offering (1 Kings 18:36) and why Daniel dates a vision by it (Daniel 9:21).

About 2.2 litres of fine flour, roughly two kilograms, which is the same measure as the omer of manna that fed one person for a day (Exodus 16:16,36). So the grain offering with each lamb is one person's daily bread. The full ephah is about 22 litres, close to two thirds of a bushel.

A hin is about 3.7 litres, so a quarter hin is a little under a litre: that much beaten oil mixed into the flour, and that much wine poured out as a drink offering with each lamb (28:5,7). The amounts step up with the animal, half a hin with a bull and a third with a ram (28:14). Oil and wine were not extras in that economy; with grain they were the three staple products of the land.

The wine was poured out at the altar and not drunk by anyone. It is the only offering that is simply lost, which is what makes it a picture Paul reaches for when he says he is being poured out like a drink offering (Philippians 2:17; 2 Timothy 4:6). The instruction here is that fermented drink, not juice, was used.

Israel's months ran on the moon, and a new month began when the crescent was first sighted after the dark, which is why chodesh, month, comes from the word for new. The new moon carried its own offering of two bulls, one ram, seven lambs and a goat (28:11-15), and it was a marked day in ordinary life: Saul holds a feast at the new moon (1 Samuel 20:5), and it is paired with the sabbath in Isaiah 1:13 and Amos 8:5.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands Moses to instruct Israel on prescribed offerings: daily burnt offerings of two lambs, additional offerings on Sabbaths and new moons, and specific burnt offerings for Passover, the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and the Festival of Weeks, each with accompanying grain and drink offerings.

headings.text: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 29
summaryBullets: “On the first day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you must not do any regular work. This will be a day for you to sound the trumpets. (29:1).
As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:2).
together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram, (29:3).
and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven male lambs. (29:4).
Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you. (29:5).
These are in addition to the monthly and daily burnt offerings with their prescribed grain offerings and drink offerings. They are a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD. (29:6).
On the tenth day of this seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you shall humble yourselves; you must not do any work. (29:7).
Present as a pleasing aroma to the LORD a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:8).
together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram, (29:9).
and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs. (29:10).
Include one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings. (29:11).
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work, and you shall observe a feast to the LORD for seven days. (29:12).
As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a food offering, a burnt offering of thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:13).
along with the grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil with each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths of an ephah with each of the two rams, (29:14).
and a tenth of an ephah with each of the fourteen lambs. (29:15).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:16).
On the second day you are to present twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:17).
along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed. (29:18).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:19).
On the third day you are to present eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:20).
along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed. (29:21).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:22).
On the fourth day you are to present ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:23).
along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed. (29:24).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:25).
On the fifth day you are to present nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:26).
along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed. (29:27).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:28).
On the sixth day you are to present eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:29).
along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed. (29:30).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:31).
On the seventh day you are to present seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:32).
along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed. (29:33).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:34).
On the eighth day you are to hold a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work. (29:35).
As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a food offering, a burnt offering of one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished, (29:36).
along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed. (29:37).
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. (29:38).

You are to present these offerings to the LORD at your appointed times, in addition to your vow and freewill offerings, whether burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings.” (29:39).
So Moses spoke all this to the Israelites just as the LORD had commanded him. (29:40).
crossRefs: Leviticus 23:23-25: The first day of the seventh month, a day of rest announced with trumpet blasts.
Leviticus 16:29-31: On the tenth day of the seventh month you must humble yourselves and do no work at all.
Leviticus 23:33-43: The Feast of Booths kept seven days in shelters, with an eighth day of assembly.
Nehemiah 8:14-18: Israel keeps the Feast of Booths in shelters, as had not been done since the days of Joshua.
John 7:37-38: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stands and calls out to anyone who is thirsty.

translationNotes.note: Three of the year's appointed times fall in this one month: a sacred assembly on the first day, the Day of Atonement on the tenth, and the seven days of Booths from the fifteenth. It lands in September or October, at the end of the dry season and the close of the agricultural year, when the grain, wine and oil are all in and before the early rains begin the next round of ploughing.

Leviticus 23:24 names the first day of the seventh month a memorial of teru'ah, the short broken blast; Numbers 29:1 calls it a day of blowing the trumpets. That is the whole description the law gives it. Its later name, Rosh Hashanah, and its use as a new year date come from usage that developed after these texts.

The Hebrew is afflict your souls, and it is the standard idiom for fasting, as Isaiah 58:3-5 makes clear when it uses the same phrase for going without food. It is the law's only commanded fast, on the tenth day of the seventh month. Acts 27:9 refers to it simply as the Fast, assuming every reader knows which one.

The bulls of the Feast of Booths count down one a day: thirteen on the first day, twelve on the second, and so on to seven on the seventh, which totals exactly seventy. No other feast has a descending sequence. The eighth day then drops to a single bull, one ram and seven lambs, matching a small ordinary festival day rather than the great week before it.

The word means a holding back or a closing gathering, from a verb meaning to restrain. It marks the last day of a festival cycle: the eighth day after Booths here, and the seventh day of Unleavened Bread at Deuteronomy 16:8. It is a day whose whole content is stopping, which is why the offering shrinks and no work is done.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands the Israelites to observe sacred assemblies in the seventh month: trumpet day on the first day, Day of Atonement on the tenth day, and the seven-day Festival of Tabernacles beginning on the fifteenth day, each with specified burnt offerings, grain offerings, and sin offerings. Moses reports these commands to Israel.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 30
summaryBullets: Then Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded: (30:1).
If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised. (30:2).
And if a woman in her father’s house during her youth makes a vow to the LORD or obligates herself by a pledge, (30:3).
and her father hears about her vow or pledge but says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. (30:4).

But if her father prohibits her on the day he hears about it, then none of the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her. (30:5).
If a woman marries while under a vow or rash promise by which she has bound herself, (30:6).
and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her on that day, then the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. (30:7).
But if her husband prohibits her when he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her or the rash promise she has made, and the LORD will absolve her. (30:8).
Every vow a widow or divorced woman pledges to fulfill is binding on her. (30:9).
If a woman in her husband’s house has made a vow or put herself under an obligation with an oath, (30:10).
and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her and does not prohibit her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. (30:11).

But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether her vows or pledges, shall stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will absolve her. (30:12).
Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow or any sworn pledge to deny herself. (30:13).

But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all the vows and pledges that bind her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard about them. (30:14).
But if he nullifies them after he hears of them, then he will bear her iniquity.” (30:15).
These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the relationship between a man and his wife, and between a father and a young daughter still in his home. (30:16).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 23:21-23: When you make a vow, do not delay in fulfilling it; if you refrain from vowing, that is no sin.
Ecclesiastes 5:4-5: It is better not to vow than to vow and not fulfil it.
Judges 11:30-39: Jephthah makes a rash vow before battle and it costs him his daughter.
1 Samuel 1:11,24-28: Hannah's vow, and its fulfilment when she brings the boy to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.
Matthew 5:33-37: Do not swear at all; let your yes be yes and your no be no.

translationNotes.note: Two different undertakings. A neder is a positive promise to give or do something, usually an offering. An issar is a binding restriction a person puts on themselves, going without something, which is why verse 13 links it to denying oneself. The Nazirite vow of chapter 6 is both at once. Both were legally enforceable, which is why this chapter exists.

translationNotes.term: He must not break his word
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא יַחֵל דְּבָרוֹ (lo yachel devaro), he shall not profane his word
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew verb is the one used for profaning something holy. A man's spoken undertaking is treated as a sacred object he can desecrate, which is a stronger idea than breaking a promise. In a world with almost no written contracts, an oath was the enforcement mechanism, and that is why Scripture takes false swearing so seriously.

translationNotes.term: On the day he hears of it
translationNotes.note: The window for a father or husband to cancel a vow is a single day, the day he learns of it (30:5,8,12). Silence past that day confirms it permanently. And if he cancels it late, after having already let it stand, verse 15 puts the liability on him: he bears her guilt. The rule protects the woman from being bound to something the household cannot honour, and it stops a man from using the power casually.

Verse 9 states the exception without qualification: whatever a widow or a divorced woman binds herself to stands. She is answerable to no father and no husband and her word is her own. Anna in Luke 2:36-37 is a widow living permanently at the temple in fasting and prayer, which is the kind of standing commitment this verse leaves open to her.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses conveys laws about vows; a man's vow is binding on him, but a father can void his unmarried daughter's vows and a husband can void his wife's vows if he forbids them when he hears of them, while a widow's or divorced woman's vows always stand.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 31
summaryBullets: And the LORD said to Moses, (31:1).
“Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites. After that, you will be gathered to your people.” (31:2).
So Moses told the people, “Arm some of your men for war, that they may go against the Midianites and execute the LORD’s vengeance on them. (31:3).
Send into battle a thousand men from each tribe of Israel.” (31:4).
So a thousand men were recruited from each tribe of Israel— twelve thousand armed for war. (31:5).
And Moses sent the thousand from each tribe into battle, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took with him the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for signaling. (31:6).
Then they waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they killed every male. (31:7).
Among the slain were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba— the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword. (31:8).
The Israelites captured the Midianite women and their children, and they plundered all their herds, flocks, and goods. (31:9).
Then they burned all the cities where the Midianites had lived, as well as all their encampments, (31:10).
and carried away all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals. (31:11).
They brought the captives, spoils, and plunder to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of Israel at the camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho. (31:12).
And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went to meet them outside the camp. (31:13).
But Moses was angry with the officers of the army — the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds — who were returning from the battle. (31:14).
“Have you spared all the women?” he asked them. (31:15).
“Look, these women caused the sons of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to turn unfaithfully against the LORD at Peor, so that the plague struck the congregation of the LORD. (31:16).
So now, kill all the boys, as well as every woman who has had relations with a man, (31:17).
but spare for yourselves every girl who has never had relations with a man. (31:18).

All of you who have killed a person or touched the dead are to remain outside the camp for seven days. On the third day and the seventh day you are to purify both yourselves and your captives. (31:19).
And purify every garment and leather good, everything made of goat’s hair, and every article of wood.” (31:20).
Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, “This is the statute of the law which the LORD has commanded Moses: (31:21).
Only the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead— (31:22).

everything that can withstand the fire— must be put through the fire, and it will be clean. But it must still be purified with the water of purification. And everything that cannot withstand the fire must pass through the water. (31:23).
On the seventh day you are to wash your clothes, and you will be clean. After that you may enter the camp.” (31:24).
The LORD said to Moses, (31:25).
“You and Eleazar the priest and the family heads of the congregation are to take a count of what was captured, both of man and beast. (31:26).
Then divide the captives between the troops who went out to battle and the rest of the congregation. (31:27).
Set aside a tribute for the LORD from what belongs to the soldiers who went into battle: one out of every five hundred, whether persons, cattle, donkeys, or sheep. (31:28).
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the LORD. (31:29).

From the Israelites’ half, take one out of every fifty, whether persons, cattle, donkeys, sheep, or other animals, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD.” (31:30).
So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses, (31:31).
and this plunder remained from the spoils the soldiers had taken: 675,000 sheep, (31:32).
and 32,000 women who had not slept with a man. (31:35).
This was the half portion for those who had gone to war: 337,500 sheep, (31:36).
including a tribute to the LORD of 675, (31:37).
36,000 cattle, including a tribute to the LORD of 72, (31:38).
30,500 donkeys, including a tribute to the LORD of 61, (31:39).
and 16,000 people, including a tribute to the LORD of 32. (31:40).
Moses gave the tribute to Eleazar the priest as an offering for the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses. (31:41).
From the Israelites’ half, which Moses had set apart from the men who had gone to war, (31:42).
this half belonged to the congregation: 337,500 sheep, (31:43).
From the Israelites’ half, Moses took one out of every fifty persons and animals and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded him. (31:47).
Then the officers who were over the units of the army — the commanders of thousands and of hundreds — approached Moses (31:48).
and said, “Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one of us is missing. (31:49).
So we have brought to the LORD an offering of the gold articles each man acquired— armlets, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces— to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD.” (31:50).
So Moses and Eleazar the priest received from them all the articles made out of gold. (31:51).
All the gold that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds presented as an offering to the LORD weighed 16,750 shekels. (31:52).
Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself. (31:53).
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD. (31:54).
crossRefs: Numbers 25:16-18: The LORD orders this campaign and states the reason for it, that Midian assailed Israel deceitfully in the matter of Peor, which is the same reason Moses gives at 31:16.
Numbers 25:1-9: The Peor affair itself, where Israelite men were drawn into the sacrifices of Baal of Peor and twenty-four thousand died in the plague.
Joshua 13:21-22: Balaam son of Beor is killed alongside the five princes of Midian, who are listed there by name as Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
1 Samuel 30:21-25: David rules that the man who stays with the baggage takes the same share as the man who fights, the same split of the spoil commanded at 31:27.
Numbers 19:11-19: The seven-day purification for anyone who touches a dead body, the rule the returning army is put under at 31:19-24.

translationNotes.note: Verse 16 gives the reason in one sentence, and it is not a land dispute or a raid. On Balaam's advice the Midianite women were used to draw Israelite men into the cult at Peor, which killed 24,000 people in the plague of chapter 25. Midian had sat in Balak's council in 22:4 and 22:7 and had gone on after the hired curse failed. The campaign answers a religious operation, and the text says so.

translationNotes.term: Phinehas with the vessels and the trumpets
translationNotes.note: The army goes out with a priest rather than with Moses, and the priest carries the holy vessels and the silver trumpets (31:6). Numbers 10:9 had set that out as the standing rule: when you go to war, sound the trumpets. Phinehas is the man who ended the Peor plague, so the officer sent is the one the episode already involved.

translationNotes.term: Purify yourselves on the third and seventh day
translationNotes.note: The whole army camps outside for seven days because everyone who has killed or touched a dead body is unclean (31:19). Clothing, leather, goat hair and wood are all washed. Metal that can take heat is passed through fire and then through the water of purification; what cannot take fire is put through the water only (31:22-23). This is the red heifer rite of chapter 19 applied at the scale of twelve thousand men.

Gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead (31:22) is the complete metal inventory of that world, and the list is worth reading as an economic record. Bronze is copper alloyed with tin, and tin had to be brought from very far away, which is why a tin ingot found in a Late Bronze Age shipwreck off the Turkish coast represents trade running most of the length of the known world.

Half to the twelve thousand who fought, half to the whole congregation who did not. From the soldiers' half, one part in 500 went to the priests; from the congregation's half, one in 50 went to the Levites (31:27-30). The arithmetic in verses 36 to 47 checks: 337,500 sheep yields a tribute of 675, and 36,000 cattle yields 72. David later makes the equal-share principle a permanent statute in Israel (1 Samuel 30:24-25).

The officers' offering of armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and beads weighed 16,750 sanctuary shekels (31:52), which at about 11.4 grams a shekel is close to 191 kilograms, or 420 pounds, of gold. Before coinage, jewellery was wealth held in wearable form and valued by weight, so this is a treasury, not a jewellery box.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses sends twelve thousand Israelite soldiers to attack Midian; they kill all the men including the five Midianite kings and Balaam, capture the women and children, and burn the settlements. The plunder is divided between the soldiers and the community, with portions designated as tribute to the LORD and for the Levites, and the commanders present gold articles as an offering.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 32
summaryBullets: Now the Reubenites and Gadites, who had very large herds and flocks, surveyed the lands of Jazer and Gilead, and they saw that the region was suitable for livestock. (32:1).
So the Gadites and Reubenites came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, and said, (32:2).
“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon, (32:3).
which the LORD conquered before the congregation of Israel, are suitable for livestock — and your servants have livestock.” (32:4).
“If we have found favor in your sight,” they said, “let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.” (32:5).
But Moses asked the Gadites and Reubenites, “Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here? (32:6).
Why are you discouraging the Israelites from crossing into the land that the LORD has given them? (32:7).
This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land. (32:8).
For when your fathers went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, they discouraged the Israelites from entering the land that the LORD had given them. (32:9).
So the anger of the LORD was kindled that day, and He swore an oath, saying, (32:10).
‘Because they did not follow Me wholeheartedly, not one of the men twenty years of age or older who came out of Egypt will see the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob— (32:11).
not one except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun— because they did follow the LORD wholeheartedly.’ (32:12).
The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation who had done evil in His sight was gone. (32:13).
Now behold, you, a brood of sinners, have risen up in place of your fathers to further stoke the burning anger of the LORD against Israel. (32:14).
For if you turn away from following Him, He will once again leave this people in the wilderness, and you will be the cause of their destruction.” (32:15).
Then the Gadites and Reubenites approached Moses and said, “We want to build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our little ones. (32:16).

But we will arm ourselves and be ready to go ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them into their place. Meanwhile, our little ones will remain in the fortified cities for protection from the inhabitants of the land. (32:17).
We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has taken possession of his inheritance. (32:18).
Yet we will not have an inheritance with them across the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on the east side of the Jordan.” (32:19).
Moses replied, “If you will do this— if you will arm yourselves before the LORD for battle, (32:20).
and if every one of your armed men crosses the Jordan before the LORD, until He has driven His enemies out before Him, (32:21).
then when the land is subdued before the LORD, you may return and be free of obligation to the LORD and to Israel. And this land will belong to you as a possession before the LORD. (32:22).
But if you do not do this, you will certainly sin against the LORD — and be assured that your sin will find you out. (32:23).
Build cities for your little ones and folds for your flocks, but do what you have promised.” (32:24).
The Gadites and Reubenites said to Moses, “Your servants will do just as our lord commands. (32:25).
Our children, our wives, our livestock, and all our animals will remain here in the cities of Gilead. (32:26).
But your servants are equipped for war, and every man will cross over to the battle before the LORD, just as our lord says.” (32:27).
So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the family leaders of the tribes of Israel. (32:28).

And Moses said to them, “If the Gadites and Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, with every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you are to give them the land of Gilead as a possession. (32:29).
But if they do not arm themselves and go across with you, then they must accept their possession among you in the land of Canaan.” (32:30).
The Gadites and Reubenites replied, “As the LORD has spoken to your servants, so we will do. (32:31).
We will cross over into the land of Canaan armed before the LORD, that we may have our inheritance on this side of the Jordan.” (32:32).

So Moses gave to the Gadites, to the Reubenites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan — the land including its cities and the territory surrounding them. (32:33).
And the Gadites built up Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer, (32:34).
Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah, (32:35).
Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran as fortified cities, and they built folds for their flocks. (32:36).
The Reubenites built up Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim, (32:37).
as well as Nebo and Baal-meon (whose names were changed), and Sibmah. And they renamed the cities they rebuilt. (32:38).
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there. (32:39).
So Moses gave Gilead to the clan of Machir son of Manasseh, and they settled there. (32:40).
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair. (32:41).
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah, after his own name. (32:42).
crossRefs: Joshua 22:1-9: Joshua releases the eastern tribes to go home once the land west of the Jordan is subdued.
Joshua 22:10-34: The altar they build by the Jordan almost starts a war until they explain what it is for.
Deuteronomy 3:12-20: Moses gives the same territory and repeats the condition that their fighting men cross over first.
Joshua 4:12-13: About forty thousand armed men of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh cross over ready for battle.
1 Chronicles 5:25-26: The eastern tribes are the first carried into exile, deported by the king of Assyria.

translationNotes.note: Gilead is the upland east of the Jordan, roughly between the Yarmuk and the northern edge of Moab, high enough to catch rain off the Mediterranean and covered in oak woodland and open grazing. It was known for balm (Jeremiah 8:22). Verse 1 gives the whole reason for the request in one clause: the Reubenites and Gadites had very large herds, and this was the best pasture they had seen.

Dry stone walls built in a ring, often against a cliff or around a cave mouth, high enough to keep animals in and predators out, with one gap as a gate that the shepherd lay across at night. Thousands survive across the Transjordan uplands. Building folds first and cities second, as verse 16 does, is the correct order of work for a herding people.

The word means stripped down or equipped, and it describes a man ready to fight without baggage, the shock troops who went at the front. Joshua 6:7 uses it of the armed men who went before the ark at Jericho. The condition Moses sets is not that they send a contingent but that they go in the vanguard, ahead of everyone else, and not come home until the last tribe has its land.

Verse 38 notes in passing that Nebo and Baal-meon were renamed. Both names carried a foreign god: Nebo is the Babylonian god Nabu, and Baal-meon means lord of the dwelling. Renaming captured towns to strip out the old god's name is a real practice, and Exodus 23:13 commands not even to speak the names of other gods.

The towns the Gadites build in verse 34 are named on an outside monument. The Moabite Stone, set up by King Mesha about 840 BC and found at Dhiban in 1868, says that the men of Gad had lived in the land of Ataroth from of old, and records Mesha taking it, along with Nebo and Dibon which appear in this same list. A Moabite king writing his own victory record confirms who his neighbours were.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Reubenites and Gadites request the lands east of the Jordan for their livestock instead of crossing over; after Moses warns them against discouraging Israel like their fathers did, they agree to fight alongside Israel in Canaan before settling in Gilead, and Moses grants them the conquered territories of Sihon and Og.

headings.text: The Tribes East of the Jordan

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 33
summaryBullets: These are the journeys of the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron. (33:1).
At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey. These are the stages listed by their starting points: (33:2).
On the fifteenth day of the first month, on the day after the Passover, the Israelites set out from Rameses. They marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians, (33:3).
who were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them; for the LORD had executed judgment against their gods. (33:4).
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth. (33:5).
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness. (33:6).
They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and they camped near Migdol. (33:7).
They set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea, into the wilderness, and they journeyed three days into the Wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah. (33:8).
They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there. (33:9).
They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea. (33:10).
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the Desert of Sin. (33:11).
They set out from the Desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah. (33:12).
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush. (33:13).
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink. (33:14).
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the Wilderness of Sinai. (33:15).
They set out from the Wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah. (33:16).
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth. (33:17).
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah. (33:18).
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez. (33:19).
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah. (33:20).
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah. (33:21).
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah. (33:22).
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher. (33:23).
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah. (33:24).
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth. (33:25).
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath. (33:26).
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah. (33:27).
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah. (33:28).
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah. (33:29).
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth. (33:30).
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan. (33:31).
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad. (33:32).
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah. (33:33).
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah. (33:34).
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber. (33:35).
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin. (33:36).
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the outskirts of the land of Edom. (33:37).
At the LORD’s command, Aaron the priest climbed Mount Hor and died there on the first day of the fifth month, in the fortieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt. (33:38).
Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor. (33:39).
Now the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming. (33:40).
And the Israelites set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah. (33:41).
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon. (33:42).
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth. (33:43).
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim on the border of Moab. (33:44).
They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad. (33:45).
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim. (33:46).
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim facing Nebo. (33:47).
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho. (33:48).
And there on the plains of Moab they camped by the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim. (33:49).
On the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses, (33:50).
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan, (33:51).
you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land, destroy all their carved images and cast idols, and demolish all their high places. (33:52).
You are to take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess. (33:53).

And you are to divide the land by lot according to your clans. Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one. Whatever falls to each one by lot will be his. You will receive an inheritance according to the tribes of your fathers. (33:54).

But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, those you allow to remain will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides; they will harass you in the land where you settle. (33:55).
And then I will do to you what I had planned to do to them.” (33:56).
crossRefs: Exodus 12:37-38: Israel sets out from Rameses to Succoth, about 600,000 men on foot besides women and children.
Exodus 14:1-2: Camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, opposite Baal-zephon.
Exodus 15:22-27: The bitter water at Marah, and then Elim with its twelve springs and seventy palm trees.
Deuteronomy 7:1-5: Tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones and cut down their Asherah poles.
Judges 2:1-3: Because you did not drive them out, they will be thorns in your sides and their gods a snare to you.

translationNotes.note: The chapter lists forty-two places in order, from Rameses to the plains of Moab, and verse 2 says Moses wrote them down at the LORD's command. It is a travel register of the kind kept by armies and caravans, recording each night's stop. Many of the names appear nowhere else and cannot now be placed on a map, which is what happens to a route log when the waypoints are wells and camps rather than towns.

Verse 4 says the plagues were executed against Egypt's gods, repeating Exodus 12:12. Each Egyptian god had a domain, the Nile, the sun, cattle, the harvest, the firstborn of the royal house, and the plagues struck across exactly those. Israel walked out while Egypt was burying its firstborn, and the text frames the whole thing as a contest already settled.

Twelve springs and seventy palm trees (33:9), which is a specific and useful description rather than a scenic one. A caravan needed water and shade in that quantity, and date palms meant food as well. The numbers are recorded because they told a traveller what the site could support.

Verse 52 lists three things to destroy: carved figures, cast metal images, and the bamot, the open-air worship platforms on the hilltops. These were not private property but public installations, an altar and often a standing stone and a wooden pole on a ridge. The command is to dismantle the infrastructure, and Judges 2:1-3 records what followed from leaving it standing.

The Hebrew is barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, taken from the hazards of that country: thorn scrub that catches a walker and blinds livestock pushing through it. Joshua 23:13 repeats it as splinters in your eyes. The image is of an injury that never quite heals and cannot be ignored.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses records the Israelites' journey from Egypt in forty-two stages, ending at the plains of Moab by the Jordan; there the LORD instructs them to drive out the Canaanites, destroy their idols, and distribute the land by lot among their tribes.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 34
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (34:1).
“Command the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan, it will be allotted to you as an inheritance with these boundaries: (34:2).
Your southern border will extend from the Wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom. On the east, your southern border will run from the end of the Salt Sea, (34:3).
cross south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, continue to Zin, and go south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go on to Hazar-addar and proceed to Azmon, (34:4).
where it will turn from Azmon, join the Brook of Egypt, and end at the Sea. (34:5).
Your western border will be the coastline of the Great Sea; this will be your boundary on the west. (34:6).
Your northern border will run from the Great Sea directly to Mount Hor, (34:7).
and from Mount Hor to Lebo-hamath, then extend to Zedad, (34:8).
continue to Ziphron, and end at Hazar-enan. This will be your boundary on the north. (34:9).
And your eastern border will run straight from Hazar-enan to Shepham, (34:10).
then go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain and continue along the slopes east of the Sea of Chinnereth. (34:11).
Then the border will go down along the Jordan and end at the Salt Sea. This will be your land, defined by its borders on all sides.” (34:12).
So Moses commanded the Israelites, “Apportion this land by lot as an inheritance. The LORD has commanded that it be given to the nine and a half tribes. (34:13).
For the tribes of the Reubenites and Gadites, along with the half-tribe of Manasseh, have already received their inheritance. (34:14).
These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, toward the sunrise.” (34:15).
Then the LORD said to Moses, (34:16).
“These are the names of the men who are to assign the land as an inheritance for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun. (34:17).
Appoint one leader from each tribe to distribute the land. (34:18).
These are their names: Caleb son of Jephunneh from the tribe of Judah; (34:19).
Shemuel son of Ammihud from the tribe of Simeon; (34:20).
Elidad son of Chislon from the tribe of Benjamin; (34:21).
Bukki son of Jogli, a leader from the tribe of Dan; (34:22).
Hanniel son of Ephod, a leader from the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph; (34:23).
Kemuel son of Shiphtan, a leader from the tribe of Ephraim; (34:24).
Eli-zaphan son of Parnach, a leader from the tribe of Zebulun; (34:25).
Paltiel son of Azzan, a leader from the tribe of Issachar; (34:26).
Ahihud son of Shelomi, a leader from the tribe of Asher; (34:27).
and Pedahel son of Ammihud, a leader from the tribe of Naphtali.” (34:28).
These are the ones whom the LORD commanded to apportion the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan. (34:29).
crossRefs: Genesis 15:18-21: The land promised to Abraham's offspring, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates.
Joshua 15:1-4: Judah's southern boundary traced by the same landmarks: Zin, Akrabbim and the Brook of Egypt.
Ezekiel 47:15-20: The boundaries of the land described again for the restored allotment.
Joshua 19:51: The allotment finished by Eleazar, Joshua and the family heads at the entrance to the tent at Shiloh.
Numbers 32:33: The territory east of the Jordan already given to Reuben, Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh.

translationNotes.note: The Mediterranean, the only sea in the region large enough to need no other name. Israel had almost no natural harbours on that coast and never became a sailing people; the ports that mattered, Tyre and Sidon, were Phoenician. That is why the sea functions in Scripture mainly as a western boundary and as a picture of what cannot be crossed.

The Dead Sea, whose surface is more than 400 metres below sea level, the lowest exposed ground on earth. It has no outlet, so everything the Jordan carries in stays and evaporates, leaving water so dense with salt and minerals that nothing lives in it. The salt on its shores was quarried in blocks and is the ordinary supply behind every mention of salt in the law.

Not the Nile. This is a wadi, a seasonal streambed, generally identified with the Wadi el-Arish, which runs north across northern Sinai to the Mediterranean and is dry for most of the year. It marks the southwestern limit of the land in 1 Kings 8:65 and Isaiah 27:12, and it was the practical frontier between Canaan and Egyptian territory.

The northern limit, at the entrance to the territory of Hamath on the Orontes, in the corridor between the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon ranges. Older versions render it the entrance of Hamath, treating levo as the common noun. It is the same northern marker the spies reached in 13:21 and the limit of Solomon's realm in 1 Kings 8:65.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַעֲלֵה עַקְרַבִּים (Ma'aleh Aqrabbim), scorpion pass
translationNotes.note: The name means scorpion ascent, a steep climb out of the Arabah south of the Dead Sea. Boundary descriptions in this chapter are made of exactly this kind of feature: a pass, a spring, a wadi, a ridge, named for what is there. There were no surveyed lines, so a border was a list of landmarks a local could walk you along.

stories.keyTakeaway: God describes Canaan's boundaries to Moses from the southern desert to the Mediterranean, and appoints Eleazar and Joshua along with one leader from each of the nine-and-a-half tribes to distribute the land by lot.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 35
summaryBullets: Again the LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho: (35:1).
“Command the Israelites to give, from the inheritance they will possess, cities for the Levites to live in and pasturelands around the cities. (35:2).
The cities will be for them to live in, and the pasturelands will be for their herds, their flocks, and all their other livestock. (35:3).
The pasturelands around the cities you are to give the Levites will extend a thousand cubits from the wall on every side. (35:4).

You are also to measure two thousand cubits outside the city on the east, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west, and two thousand on the north, with the city in the center. These areas will serve as larger pasturelands for the cities. (35:5).
Six of the cities you give the Levites are to be appointed as cities of refuge, to which a manslayer may flee. In addition to these, give the Levites forty-two other cities. (35:6).
The total number of cities you give the Levites will be forty-eight, with their corresponding pasturelands. (35:7).

The cities that you apportion from the territory of the Israelites should be given to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one.” (35:8).
Then the LORD said to Moses, (35:9).
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan, (35:10).
designate cities to serve as your cities of refuge, so that a person who kills someone unintentionally may flee there. (35:11).
You are to have these cities as a refuge from the avenger, so that the manslayer will not die until he stands trial before the assembly. (35:12).
The cities you select will be your six cities of refuge. (35:13).
Select three cities across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan as cities of refuge. (35:14).
These six cities will serve as a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there. (35:15).
If, however, anyone strikes a person with an iron object and kills him, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death. (35:16).
Or if anyone has in his hand a stone of deadly size, and he strikes and kills another, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death. (35:17).
If anyone has in his hand a deadly object of wood, and he strikes and kills another, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death. (35:18).
The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him. (35:19).
Likewise, if anyone maliciously pushes another or intentionally throws an object at him and kills him, (35:20).

or if in hostility he strikes him with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death; he is a murderer. When the avenger of blood finds the murderer, he is to kill him. (35:21).
But if anyone pushes a person suddenly, without hostility, or throws an object at him unintentionally, (35:22).
or without looking drops a heavy stone that kills him, but he was not an enemy and did not intend to harm him, (35:23).
then the congregation must judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances. (35:24).

The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood. Then the assembly will return him to the city of refuge to which he fled, and he must live there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil. (35:25).
But if the manslayer ever goes outside the limits of the city of refuge to which he fled (35:26).
and the avenger of blood finds him outside of his city of refuge and kills him, then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed, (35:27).
because the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. Only after the death of the high priest may he return to the land he owns. (35:28).
This will be a statutory ordinance for you for the generations to come, wherever you live. (35:29).
If anyone kills a person, the murderer is to be put to death on the testimony of the witnesses. But no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness. (35:30).
You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death. (35:31).
Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge and allow him to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest. (35:32).
Do not pollute the land where you live, for bloodshed pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it. (35:33).
Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (35:34).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 4:41-43: Moses sets apart Bezer, Ramoth in Gilead, and Golan in Bashan east of the Jordan, the first three of the six cities commanded here.
Joshua 20:7-9: Kedesh, Shechem, and Hebron are set apart west of the Jordan, and the manslayer states his case in the gate before the elders before the city takes him in.

Deuteronomy 19:15-21: The same procedure spelled out for the courtroom, where both parties stand before the priests and the judges, the judges investigate thoroughly, and only after that comes life for life, eye for eye.
Leviticus 19:18: The same law forbids revenge and grudge-bearing outright, which is exactly what the avenger of blood is held back from until the assembly has judged between him and the killer.
Deuteronomy 32:35: 'Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,' says the LORD, later in the same law that puts the congregation between the killer and the avenger here.

translationNotes.note: Six towns, three east of the Jordan and three west, spaced so that anyone in the land could reach one (35:13-14). They exist for the man who kills without intent, and the point is a trial: he runs to the city, and the assembly then judges between him and the avenger (35:12,24). Without them the only outcome was a killing at the roadside before anyone asked what happened. Deuteronomy 19:3 adds that the roads to them were to be kept passable.

The eastern city of refuge for Reuben, on the open tableland east of the Dead Sea (Deuteronomy 4:43). It is named on an outside monument: the Moabite Stone, a victory inscription of King Mesha of Moab found at Dhiban in 1868 and dated to about 840 BC, says in line 27 that he built Bezer, for it lay in ruins. A town a reader would otherwise skip past turns out to be a real place that changed hands and was rebuilt.

The other two eastern cities. Golan sat in Bashan, the high grazing plateau northeast of the Sea of Galilee, and its name still marks the Golan Heights. Ramoth-Gilead stood on the eastern frontier and was fought over for generations between Israel and Aram; Ahab dies attacking it (1 Kings 22:29-37) and Jehu is anointed king there (2 Kings 9:1-6).

The go'el is the nearest adult male relative, the same office that buys back family land (Leviticus 25:25) and marries a childless widow (Ruth 4). One of his duties was to answer a killing in the family. This law does not abolish him; it puts a court between him and the man he is pursuing. Verse 27 keeps his old right alive outside the city limits, which is why leaving is fatal.

translationNotes.term: Until the death of the high priest
translationNotes.note: The manslayer stays inside the city until the high priest dies, and then goes home free (35:25,28). It is not a fixed sentence: the term is however long that man lives, so the length depends on who is in office when the death happened. Verses 31 and 32 rule out buying out of it, just as they rule out a ransom for a murderer's life.

translationNotes.term: A thousand cubits and two thousand
translationNotes.note: A cubit is about 44.5 centimetres, the length from elbow to fingertip. The Levites' pasture runs a thousand cubits out from the town wall, about 445 metres, and the outer square is measured two thousand cubits on each side, about 890 metres, with the town in the middle (35:4-5). That belt of land was for their herds, since they had no tribal territory to graze.

translationNotes.term: One word for murderer and manslayer
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רֹצֵחַ (rotseach), one who takes a life - בִּשְׁגָגָה (bishgagah), unintentionally
translationNotes.note: Hebrew does not have a separate noun for the murderer and the man who kills by accident. Numbers 35:11 applies rotseach to the man who strikes someone down bishgagah, unintentionally, and tells him to run; 35:25 uses the same noun for the man the congregation rescues from the avenger; 35:16 uses it of the killer who is executed. English 'homicide' has the same range. Because one word covers both, the chapter has to supply tests, and 35:16-23 is those tests.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כְּלִי בַרְזֶל (kli barzel), an iron object - בְּאֵיבָה (be-eivah), in enmity - בִּצְדִיָּה (bitsdiyah), lying in wait
translationNotes.note: Numbers 35:16-21 lists what convicts a man. He struck with an iron object; or with a stone in the hand of a kind that kills; or with a wooden implement of a kind that kills; or he shoved the man in hatred; or he threw something at him while lying in wait; or he struck him with his hand in enmity. Two things run through the list, a weapon capable of killing and a prior state of hostility, and each entry ends the same way: he is a rotseach, and the murderer shall surely be put to death.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּפֶתַע בְּלֹא־אֵיבָה (befeta belo eivah), 'suddenly, without enmity' - בְּלֹא רְאוֹת (belo re'ot), 'without seeing'
translationNotes.note: Numbers 35:22-23 is the mirror image and it turns on the same two questions. He shoved him suddenly without enmity, or threw something without lying in wait, or dropped a stone on him without seeing him, and the verse closes by stating the finding directly: he was not his enemy and was not seeking his harm. Deuteronomy 19:5 gives the worked example, two men cutting timber when the iron head slips off the handle mid-swing and kills the other. Deuteronomy 19:6 states the test in one line, whether the killer hated the man beforehand.

translationNotes.term: No ransom, and never on one witness
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֹּפֶר (kopher), a ransom - עֵד אֶחָד (ed echad), a single witness
translationNotes.note: Two rules close the chapter and both cut against the powerful. Numbers 35:31 forbids taking a kopher for the life of a murderer, so a rich man cannot buy his way out of a killing; Exodus 21:30 permits exactly such a payment for the owner of a goring ox, which marks the difference between negligence and murder. Numbers 35:30 then bars execution on the testimony of one witness, a rule Deuteronomy 17:6 and 19:15 repeat. Verse 33 gives the reason the chapter will not allow a settlement: bloodshed pollutes the land, and nothing cleanses it but the blood of the man who shed it.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands the Israelites to give the Levites forty-eight towns with pasturelands, including six cities of refuge where those who kill accidentally may flee until the high priest dies. Deliberate murder requires death by the avenger; accidental killing requires assembly judgment and refuge in these cities, with no ransom permitted and no leaving before the high priest's death.

stories.title: 🐍 Numbers 36
summaryBullets: Now the family heads of the clan of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, one of the clans of Joseph, approached Moses and the leaders who were the heads of the Israelite families and addressed them, (36:1).
saying, “When the LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance to the Israelites by lot, He also commanded him to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters. (36:2).

But if they marry any of the men from the other tribes of Israel, their inheritance will be withdrawn from the portion of our fathers and added to the tribe into which they marry. So our allotted inheritance would be taken away. (36:3).
And when the Jubilee for the Israelites comes, their inheritance will be added to the tribe into which they marry and taken away from the tribe of our fathers.” (36:4).
So at the word of the LORD, Moses commanded the Israelites: “The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks correctly. (36:5).
This is what the LORD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may marry anyone they please, provided they marry within a clan of the tribe of their father. (36:6).
No inheritance in Israel may be transferred from tribe to tribe, because each of the Israelites is to retain the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers. (36:7).
Every daughter who possesses an inheritance from any Israelite tribe must marry within a clan of the tribe of her father, so that every Israelite will possess the inheritance of his fathers. (36:8).
No inheritance may be transferred from one tribe to another, for each tribe of Israel must retain its inheritance.” (36:9).
So the daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD had commanded Moses. (36:10).
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married to cousins on their father’s side. (36:11).
They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained within the tribe of their father’s clan. (36:12).
These are the commandments and ordinances that the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho. (36:13).
crossRefs: Numbers 27:1-11: The original ruling that gave Zelophehad's daughters their father's inheritance.
Leviticus 25:8-13: The fiftieth year proclaimed, when every man returns to his own property and his own clan.
1 Kings 21:1-4: Naboth refuses to sell his vineyard, because it is the inheritance of his fathers.
Joshua 17:3-6: Zelophehad's five daughters receive their allotment among the sons of Manasseh.
Ruth 4:5-6: The nearer kinsman declines to redeem, because it would put his own inheritance at risk.

translationNotes.note: Every fiftieth year, announced on the Day of Atonement by a ram's horn, when land sold since the last jubilee went back to the family that first held it and Israelites in debt servitude went free (Leviticus 25:8-13). The word yovel means a ram's horn. Because of it land was never really sold, only leased for the years remaining, and Leviticus 25:15-16 says the price was to be calculated on that basis.

The clan heads of Manasseh spot the gap that chapter 27 opened. If an heiress marries outside her tribe, her land goes with her to her husband's family, and at the jubilee it does not come back, because it now belongs to another tribe permanently (36:3-4). The answer is not to take her inheritance away but to limit whom she may marry, which is how verse 6 puts it: she may marry anyone she pleases within her father's tribal clan.

The five daughters marry the sons of their father's brothers (36:11). Marriage within the clan was the normal arrangement, not an emergency measure: Isaac is sent back to Abraham's family for a wife (Genesis 24:3-4), and Jacob marries Laban's daughters. It kept land, obligation and the kinsman-redeemer duty inside one extended family.

translationNotes.note: Five women named four separate times in Scripture (26:33; 27:1; 36:11; Joshua 17:3), which is more attention than most men in these lists receive. Two of the names are also places in the territory their family settled: Tirzah later served as a capital of the northern kingdom (1 Kings 15:33), and Hoglah appears on ostraca excavated at Samaria as a district name. The record kept both the women and the ground they held.

The book's closing verse fixes where all of this was given: on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho, on a valley floor about 250 metres below sea level, with the river and the walled town in sight. Israel is camped at the edge of the land, and everything from chapter 22 onward happens on that one stretch of ground.

stories.keyTakeaway: The leaders of Manasseh petition Moses about Zelophehad's daughters marrying outside the tribe and taking their inheritance with them; Moses establishes that these daughters may marry freely but only within their father's tribal clan, and Zelophehad's five daughters comply by marrying their cousins.

intro:
Numbers (Hebrew: Bemidbar, "In the wilderness") was written by Moses during Israel's forty-year wilderness period between the Exodus from Egypt (c. 1446 BC) and the people's entry into Canaan (c. 1406 BC). Moses, the prophet and lawgiver who had led the nation out of Egyptian slavery at God's command, composed the book in real time as he guided Israel through the Sinai Peninsula, the Negev, and the regions east of the Jordan. The journey crossed territory held by nomadic peoples (Amalekites, Midianites, Edomites, Moabites, Ammonites) and approached the borders of the Canaanite city-states. The setting is the Late Bronze Age, dominated to the west by Egypt's New Kingdom 18th Dynasty and to the east by the Mesopotamian powers (the Mitanni kingdom and the rising Assyrian state). Jesus and the apostles attribute the Pentateuch, including Numbers, to Moses (Mark 12:26, Luke 24:44, John 5:46, Romans 10:5).

Numbers is the fourth book of the Pentateuch (the five books of Moses). Its Hebrew name comes from the opening phrase of the book, following the ancient Jewish convention of titling books by their opening words; the English title "Numbers" comes from the Greek Septuagint translation Arithmoi (3rd century BC). Hebrew manuscript fragments of Numbers were among the Dead Sea Scrolls discovered at Qumran (mid-20th century AD), with copies dating to the 2nd and 1st centuries BC.
